status: v2 (22 Nov 2026): clusters, summaries, numbers. Draft: Aditya reviews.
setting: An invented country with its own courts and statutes. No real legal system is assumed: courts have a level, decisions relate to sources by three generic relations. All names are invented.

court.about: a court of the invented country

parts.court_type: the type of court in plain words, different for each court, e.g. District Court, Court of Appeal, Supreme Court

provision.about: a section of an invented statute

parts.statute: the statute's title in plain words, ending in Act or Ordinance, e.g. Personal Data Act; the same words for every section of one statute

attrs.summary: processing of personal data is lawful only with the data subject's freely given, specific consent, unless another lawful basis applies

decision.about: a court decision between a person and an organisation

parts.org: one plain word for the kind of organisation that is the second party, e.g. Media, Health, Bank, Insurance, Systems

attrs.facts: an employer read a worker's private messages
attrs.outcome: claim upheld; damages awarded to the worker

relies_on.meaning: the decision uses the source as a basis for its ruling

distinguishes.meaning: the decision says an earlier decision does not apply because the facts differ

rejects.meaning: the decision refuses to accept the source as a basis for its ruling

confusable_note: DRAFT for review: distinguishing an earlier decision is easily written as rejecting it; a decision that relied on a source only to reject an argument reads as both.
real_names_note: Real names that invented entities must not use (whole words, any case; world.check). Empty until Aditya approves the sources for this list. To check by hand: 'Vantor' in the law pilot ('Pell v. Vantor Systems') may be a real company name.

questions.text: Which sources did the court rely on in {s}?
Which decisions treated {o} as a valid basis, and which did not?

world_notes: Make 3 courts at different levels (shared by all clusters), 4-6 provisions of ONE invented statute for the cluster's area of law, and enough decisions (years 2010-2025) that each paper has its own mix. A decision may only rely on, distinguish or reject EARLIER decisions. Each decision is its own dispute with its own parties (no decision is an appeal of another decision in this world). Plant disagreements: two decisions that treat the same provision in opposite ways (one relies on it, one rejects it).
cluster_note: All provisions and decisions of this cluster belong to ONE area of law within the cluster topic: invent one statute for that area (all of this cluster's provisions are sections of it) and disputes that fit it.
